Internal Quality Checks!row 37 repeats the same interpretation; Deterministic Checks!row 24 names check-probe-not-in-seed.py and refers to seed data/reference markup. I read the frozen Harbor skill, quality-checks.md section 36, deterministic-checks.md's check-probe-not-in-seed.py recipe, the staged seed/reference layout, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. I built an explicit 160-value inventory covering all distinctive fixed saved titles/title variants, filenames, DOM IDs, render/log/recovery markers, timer markers, error markers, network success/refusal tokens, isolation keys and the console inspection array. I searched each literal across every file under solution/ and environment/assets/: 24 files, including compiled public/assets/index-0TNzM6xa.js, runtime sources, both runner HTML copies, all example assets, server initialization and the seed. No fixed saved title or distinctive mutation output matched any of these files. Examples absent from all 24 files include QC Example Saved Copy (Functional prompt:121), js-dispatch-ok and dispatch-handler-marker (:129-137), css-timer-fired-1/2 (:150-153), cancel-A-delayed (:174), cw-forbidden-title (:192), all error recovery markers (:272,290,313,341), level-log/level-warn/level-error/level-info (:348-351), object-check/nested-value and [11, 22, 33] (:359-361), history-first/history-second (:367-368), all S21-S24 QC titles and changed source values (:397-436), and nested-control-done/forbidden-nested-completion/shared-deadline-recovered (:448-456). This was a local literal/source check, not a claim to have run the private checker executable.

Generated values also require real creation: gates/render/judge.toml:25 directs the judge to "Choose a new distinctive marker" and says "The marker merely appearing in the editor or a hardcoded sample is insufficient." gates/constraints/judge.toml:25 creates a unique CW gate title and newly chosen marker, observes the actual write, then :27 retrieves the resulting identity and exact fields in an independent clean context; it forbids substituting an example. Functional prompt:120 similarly requires an authored edit different from the selected example, :36-38 generates the network nonce, :197 substitutes a fresh forbidden-title suffix if needed, and :401-403 requires a fresh monitor execution marker with an actual successful update/readback control. Polish prompt:43 creates its own harmless recognisable record instead of using another dimension's identity. Visual prompt:35-37 does not create mutation probes. Generic controls and method names are not distinctive saved/output sentinels.

Investigated overlap, not ignored: the only two matches in the explicit 160-value scan were the intentionally misspelled method name forEeach in solution/app/starters/broken.js:4 and starters/README.md:10. This is an example source asset and explanatory documentation, not already-rendered console output or a saved mutation record. The exact S10 source (Functional prompt:266-270) additionally introduces absent failed-partial-dom, follows newly completed latest-good-B, and requires a Run and error observation; the global instruction at :15 explicitly says to compare unique markers/counts rather than count retained history as new output. I did not treat this lexical overlap as a credible pre-satisfied mutation. The finite loop/library-language/API words are similarly not mutation sentinels.

Independent raw corroboration: raw-evidence-index.json names run-golden-20260930-092021/RESULTS.json. I recomputed its SHA256 and obtained ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09, matching that index. I checked all 22 actual_app_files hashes and both Functional prompt/judge hashes against this frozen task: zero mismatches. The raw facts.S01.startup_ready.evidence.value records hello.js, twelve square lines, logs "LOG\nprinted %d rows\n12", and manual_run_used:false; it does not contain forEeach or the authored probe outputs. facts.S10.js_error_message.evidence.results[0] later records the exact bad.js source and newLogs "\nERROR\nitems.forEeach is not a function ? line 4". I verified the executed driver copies' hashes: drivers/workspace_flow.cjs:45-48 actually snapshots initial output; drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:117 subtracts prior log text and :119-120 evaluates newly appended error/line output. These are raw scripted observations supporting initial-state/probe freshness, not a hosted Oracle score or a configured LLM-judge result.

Adversarial reasoning: a conforming app may use different built-in examples, server-rendered saved records, and its own layout; the gate's newly chosen marker and saved identity and the UI-purpose instructions do not require our reference's initial sample. A broken app that only retains a static sample or a seeded QC record cannot meet the actual newly authored Run and independent-context newly saved-record evidence. A variant that retains a previous forEeach error while doing nothing on the S10 Run cannot satisfy the explicit new-output/count requirement; the raw driver also rejects that retained-history witness. These are bounded source-level challenges, not executed mutant runs. I found no plausible false-pass/false-fail witness caused by a pre-satisfied initial mutation probe. Full configured judge timing, Oracle and target-model performance remain unmeasured and are not asserted by this row's Pass.
